title: Aximote — Vehicle
description: Live state from Prometheus; trips, charges, places and journeys from Postgres. Built for an EV — fuel panels are omitted rather than left to show nulls. Both datasources are template variables pinned to this lab's uids, and the vehicle variable names its datasource explicitly: a query variable without one inherits Grafana's default and silently returns nothing.

list.name: tz
list.label: Time zone
list.description: IANA zone for clock-time panels, e.g. Australia/Sydney

list.name: cycle
list.label: Charge cycle
list.query:
SELECT to_char(charged_at AT TIME ZONE '${tz}', 'DD Mon HH24:MI') || '  ·  ' || round(distance_km::numeric, 0) || ' km  ·  ' || trips || ' trips' AS __text,
       cycle_id AS __value
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND distance_km IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY distance_km DESC

panels.title: Energy aboard
panels.description: State of charge against the 81.5 kWh pack. Derived in PromQL rather than stored, because the API reports a percentage and a capacity but never the product.

panels.title: Odometer
panels.description: Raw odometerKm from the API. Unit is a plain suffix, not Grafana's lengthkm, which SI-scales five-figure values and renders 37556 as "37.6 K km". Cross-check it against Distance driven below: the API's trip history only goes back to Aug 2026, so the two will not agree, and a mismatch between this number and the dash reading is an upstream question for Aximote.

panels.title: State
panels.description: On trip comes from the live state. Ignition is shown too because it latches — observed true on a parked car with a two-hour-old ignition timestamp — so check its age in Reading freshness before believing it.

panels.title: Places and latest position
panels.description: Each circle is somewhere the car actually stops, clustered to ~1.1 km and labelled with its visit count — at finer granularity one driveway splits across four cells and no cluster forms. Circle size scales with visits. The red dot is the newest GPS fix regardless of the time range. The thin line is the true recorded path, which fills in slowly: a fix is stored only when the car reports a new one.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT latitude, longitude, visits, departures, arrivals,
       COALESCE(locality, '?') AS locality
FROM aximote.place
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY visits DESC

SELECT fixed_at AS "time", latitude, longitude, speed_kmh, battery_level_pct
FROM aximote.location_track
WHERE $__timeFilter(fixed_at)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY fixed_at

SELECT fixed_at AS "time", latitude, longitude, battery_level_pct, range_km,
       speed_kmh, fix_age_sec
FROM aximote.location_track
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY fixed_at DESC
LIMIT 1

panels.title: Reading freshness
panels.description: Age of each individual reading. The API timestamps them separately and they disagree by hours — a current status poll routinely carries a GPS fix that is hours old. One overall freshness number would read green while location was stale.

panels.title: Journeys — the chain of trips
panels.description: Every trip in the time range, drawn end to end in chronological order, with a dot at each endpoint sized by that trip's distance. These are straight start-to-end vectors, not driven routes: the API gives a trip only its two endpoints, no polyline. Because one trip's end is usually the next one's start, the joins between trips collapse to almost nothing and the chain reads as a single journey.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT start_time AS "time", seq, latitude, longitude,
       route, distance_km, eco_score, avg_speed_kmh
FROM aximote.trip_vector
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY start_time, seq

panels.title: Places — where the car stops
panels.description: Clustered to ~1.1 km. Typical departure and arrival clock times are what separate one cluster from another when the API labels several of them "Sydney": a place you leave at 16:53 and reach at 09:52 is work, whichever way it is named.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(p.locality, '?') AS "Place",
       round(p.latitude::numeric, 2) || ', ' || round(p.longitude::numeric, 2) AS "Coords",
       p.visits      AS "Visits",
       p.departures  AS "Out",
       p.arrivals    AS "In",
       to_char(make_interval(secs => p.avg_departure_sec), 'HH24:MI') AS "Leaves",
       to_char(make_interval(secs => p.avg_arrival_sec),   'HH24:MI') AS "Arrives",
       round(p.avg_trip_km::numeric, 1) AS "Avg trip",
       round((COALESCE(k.avg_parked_sec, 0) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1) AS "Parked h"
FROM aximote.place p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT round(latitude::numeric, 2)  AS lat,
         round(longitude::numeric, 2) AS lon,
         avg(parked_sec)              AS avg_parked_sec
  FROM aximote.parked_interval
  WHERE latitude IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1, 2
) k ON round(p.latitude::numeric, 2) = k.lat
   AND round(p.longitude::numeric, 2) = k.lon
WHERE p.vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY p.visits DESC
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Departures by hour of day
panels.description: Every trip start, bucketed by local hour. Bimodal on this data: a morning peak and a larger late-afternoon one.

targets.rawSql:
WITH hours AS (SELECT generate_series(0, 23) AS hour)
SELECT lpad(h.hour::text, 2, '0') AS "Hour",
       count(t.trip_id)           AS "Departures"
FROM hours h
LEFT JOIN aximote.trip_local t
       ON t.hour = h.hour
      AND $__timeFilter(t.start_time)
      AND t.vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
GROUP BY h.hour
ORDER BY h.hour

panels.title: First departure of the day
panels.description: Mean clock time of the day's first trip, by weekday. Distinct from the hour histogram, which a single busy day can dominate — this counts each day once, so it answers when you actually set off.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT dow_name                        AS "Day",
       avg(seconds_into_day) / 3600.0  AS "Hour of day",
       count(*)                        AS "Days"
FROM aximote.day_first_departure
WHERE $__timeFilter(local_start)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
GROUP BY dow_name, dow
ORDER BY dow

SELECT dow_name          AS "Day",
       sum(distance_km)   AS "km"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
GROUP BY dow_name, dow
ORDER BY dow

SELECT count(*) AS "trips"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.title: Distance driven
panels.description: Summed from trip history, which begins Aug 2026. Deliberately separate from the Odometer panel: the two measure different things and will not match.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(distance_km) AS "km"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

SELECT sum(duration_sec) AS "seconds"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.title: Typical park
panels.description: Median gap between one trip ending and the next beginning.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY parked_sec) AS "seconds"
FROM aximote.parked_interval
WHERE $__timeFilter(parked_from)

SELECT sum(energy_consumed_kwh) AS "kWh"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.title: CO₂ reported
panels.description: Aximote's own figure, kept because it is in the payload. For a battery EV it reflects grid intensity assumptions rather than tailpipe output, so treat it as the vendor's estimate, not a measurement.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(co2_kg) AS "kg"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.title: Cold weather costs range
panels.description: Each dot is one trip: outside temperature against energy per 100 km. On this data trips near 4 °C average 34.3 kWh/100 km against 17.6 between 15 and 25 °C — roughly double. This is the single strongest predictor of consumption in the dataset.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT outside_temperature AS "Outside °C",
       kwh_per_100km       AS "kWh/100km",
       distance_km
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND outside_temperature IS NOT NULL
  AND kwh_per_100km IS NOT NULL
  AND distance_km > 1
ORDER BY outside_temperature

panels.title: Energy per 100 km, per trip
panels.description: One point per completed trip. Short cold hops sit high; highway runs sit low.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT start_time AS "time", kwh_per_100km AS "kWh/100km"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND kwh_per_100km IS NOT NULL
  AND distance_km > 1
ORDER BY start_time

panels.title: Driving scores
panels.description: Aximote's own per-trip scores. Not status readings, so deliberately not coloured red/amber/green; each line also carries its own dash pattern so the three stay separable without relying on hue.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT start_time AS "time",
       eco_score         AS "Eco",
       speed_score       AS "Speed",
       consistency_score AS "Consistency"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY start_time

SELECT local_date       AS "day",
       sum(distance_km) AS "km"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT local_start AS "Started",
       dow_name    AS "Day",
       COALESCE(start_locality, '?') || ' → ' || COALESCE(end_locality, '?') AS "Route",
       distance_km         AS "km",
       duration_sec        AS "Duration",
       avg_speed_kmh       AS "Avg",
       energy_consumed_kwh AS "kWh",
       kwh_per_100km       AS "kWh/100km",
       eco_score           AS "Eco",
       outside_temperature AS "Outside"
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY start_time DESC

SELECT sum(cost_amount) AS "spend"
FROM aximote.refuel_session
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

SELECT sum(cost_amount) / NULLIF(sum(energy_charged_kwh), 0) AS "per kWh"
FROM aximote.refuel_session
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.title: Per 100 km
panels.description: Charge spend over distance driven, both aggregated across the selected range. A session cannot be attributed to one trip, so this is only meaningful over a window wide enough to contain both.

targets.rawSql:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT sum(cost_amount) AS cost
  FROM aximote.refuel_session
  WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
), driven AS (
  SELECT sum(distance_km) AS km
  FROM aximote.trip_local
  WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
)
SELECT 100.0 * spend.cost / NULLIF(driven.km, 0) AS "per 100km"
FROM spend, driven

panels.title: Charge efficiency
panels.description: Range added per kWh delivered, across the range. Lower than the trips' own km/kWh because it includes charging losses and whatever the car did between sessions.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(range_added_km) / NULLIF(sum(energy_charged_kwh), 0) AS "km per kWh"
FROM aximote.refuel_session
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

SELECT sum(energy_charged_kwh) AS "kWh"
FROM aximote.refuel_session
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.title: Charging now
panels.description: True while a session is open. The API marks an in-progress session isActive, which is the only live charging signal it offers.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "active"
FROM aximote.refuel
WHERE is_active IS TRUE

SELECT start_time AS "time", price_per_kwh AS "per kWh"
FROM aximote.refuel_session
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND price_per_kwh IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY start_time

panels.title: Where it charges
panels.description: Marker size is energy delivered, so a slow top-up and a DC fast stop are distinguishable at a glance.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT start_time AS "time", latitude, longitude,
       energy_charged_kwh AS added, cost_amount, avg_charging_kw,
       price_per_kwh, kind
FROM aximote.refuel_session
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY start_time

panels.title: Charge sessions
panels.description: Duration is the resolved window, which the API reports separately from the nominal one and which disagrees with it — collapsing the two would silently pick a definition of session length.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT start_time AS "Started",
       duration_sec AS "Duration",
       start_fuel_level_pct AS "From",
       end_fuel_level_pct   AS "To",
       energy_charged_kwh   AS "Added",
       avg_charging_kw      AS "Avg kW",
       range_added_km       AS "Range +",
       range_km_per_kwh     AS "km/kWh",
       cost_amount          AS "Cost",
       price_per_kwh        AS "Per kWh",
       outside_temperature  AS "Outside",
       window_source        AS "Source"
FROM aximote.refuel_session
WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY start_time DESC

panels.title: One charge — how far it got
Furthest on one charge

targets.rawSql:
SELECT max(distance_km) AS km
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.description: Total distance driven between one charge finishing and the next starting. Neither endpoint exists in the API as a single record: trips and charges are separate endpoints with no link, so the window is reconstructed from times.

panels.title: Longest single trip

targets.rawSql:
SELECT max(distance_km) AS km
FROM aximote.trip_local
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.description: The single longest uninterrupted trip on record, regardless of charge.

panels.title: Implied full-charge range

targets.rawSql:
SELECT max(implied_full_range_km) AS km
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND soc_used >= 40

panels.description: Best cycle's distance extrapolated to the whole battery. Optimistic by construction — it scales up from the part of the pack actually used — so cycles that consumed under 40% of charge are excluded as too short to extrapolate from.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT avg(distance_km) AS km
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND distance_km IS NOT NULL

SELECT count(*) AS n
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND distance_km IS NOT NULL

panels.title: Deepest discharge

targets.rawSql:
SELECT max(soc_used) AS pct
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})

panels.description: Largest state-of-charge drop between two charges.

panels.title: Distance per charge cycle
panels.description: One bar per charge, newest at the right. The open cycle — the charge you are currently running on — is included and will grow until the next charge closes it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_char(charged_at AT TIME ZONE '${tz}', 'DD Mon') AS "Charged",
       distance_km AS "km"
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE $__timeFilter(charged_at)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
  AND distance_km IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY charged_at

panels.title: Charge cycles
panels.description: Sorted by distance. SOC from/to are the levels the API reported at the two charges bracketing the cycle, so the drop includes anything the car did while parked, not just driving.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT charged_at            AS "Charged",
       soc_start             AS "From",
       soc_end               AS "To",
       distance_km           AS "km",
       trips                 AS "Trips",
       longest_trip_km       AS "Longest",
       energy_used_kwh       AS "kWh used",
       places                AS "Places",
       implied_full_range_km AS "Implied full"
FROM aximote.charge_cycle
WHERE $__timeFilter(charged_at)
  AND vehicle_name IN (${vehicle:sqlstring})
ORDER BY distance_km DESC NULLS LAST

panels.title: Where one charge went
panels.description: Every trip in the charge cycle picked above, which defaults to the furthest one, drawn as one chronological chain. Straight start-to-end vectors, not driven routes — the API gives a trip only its two endpoints.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT start_time AS "time", 1 AS seq, start_latitude AS latitude,
       start_longitude AS longitude, route, distance_km
FROM aximote.charge_cycle_trip
WHERE cycle_id = '$cycle' AND start_latitude IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT start_time, 2, end_latitude, end_longitude, route, distance_km
FROM aximote.charge_cycle_trip
WHERE cycle_id = '$cycle' AND end_latitude IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 1, 2

SELECT start_time          AS "Started",
       route               AS "Route",
       distance_km         AS "km",
       energy_consumed_kwh AS "kWh",
       avg_speed_kmh       AS "Avg",
       eco_score           AS "Eco",
       outside_temperature AS "Outside"
FROM aximote.charge_cycle_trip
WHERE cycle_id = '$cycle'
ORDER BY start_time

panels.title: Exporter
panels.description: Whether the last poll of the Aximote API succeeded. Independent of whether the car is reporting — Reading freshness is the panel for that.

panels.title: Rows stored vs polls
panels.description: History rows rise far more slowly than polls, and that is correct: a row is keyed on the car's own capture time, so polling a car that has not reported since the last poll stores nothing.
